To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding stoichiometries of anions by norbornene-based anion receptors are controlled by a combination of steric and electronic effects, with steric factors dominating in the binding of dihydrogen phosphate and electronic effects dominating in the binding by 3a and3b of the larger acetate.
The binding of dihydrogen phosphate by norbornene-based anion receptors was controlled by steric factors, while the binding of acetate was controlled both by steric and electronic effects.
(a) the binding stoichiometries of 1a–3b to dihydrogenphosphates were controlled by steric constraints and (b) the binding stoichiomety of 3a–3b was controlled by subtle, electronic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and preparation of new, charge-neutral receptors based on the norbornene framework, and with their ability to interact selectively with anions in DCM and DMSO.
developing new, charge-neutral, norbornene-based anion receptors that bind anions in DCM and DMSO.
the synthesis and application of novel receptors and their use as tools for the development of a better understanding of anion binding interactions in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding stoichiometries are controlled by a combination of steric and electronic factors.
the binding of anions by 3a and/or 3b is governed by the combination of steric and electronic factors.
the binding of acetate to 3a and to 3b is controlled by a subtle balance of electrostatic and steric interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of anion by a receptor is a subtle interplay between steric, electrostatic, and electronic effects.
the binding of acetate by 3a and/or 3b is based on a combination of both electronic factors and steric constraints.
the binding stoichiometries of anion receptors can be controlled by a combination of electronic and steric factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of anions by neutral receptors is often not as simple as one might expect.
the binding stoichiometries of receptors 3a and/or 3b to simple anions can be controlled by the electronic effects of substituents on the norbornene backbone.
the electronic effects of the norbornene substituents can be tuned to influence the binding stoichiometries of anions.
